entries.title: Squares on a right triangle
entries.subject: maths
entries.claim: On a right triangle, the squares on the two legs together cover exactly the square on the hypotenuse: 3² + 4² = 5², shown with tiles, then again for 5-12-13 and 8-15-17.
assumptions: the triangles are exact right triangles with whole-number sides (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17)
lengths are counted in tiles: a tile is a 1 × 1 × 1 cube
three cases are counted; the film does not show the theorem for every right triangle

colour_key.means: the square on the shorter leg, built from tiles (9 tiles for the 3-4-5 triangle).
the square on the longer leg (16 tiles for 3-4-5). Coral and aqua tiles together fill the square on the hypotenuse.
the right triangle itself.
the numbers and equations that count the tiles.

entries.title: A cube cut into eight blocks
entries.subject: maths
entries.claim: A cube of side a + b, cut at a along each edge, falls into eight blocks (one a³, three a²b, three ab², one b³), so (a + b)³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³ for positive lengths a and b.
assumptions: a and b are positive lengths, so the cube can be cut at a along each edge
the lengths are symbolic: there are no units, and a and b are drawn at one fixed ratio the identity does not depend on

colour_key.means: the one a × a × a block, and the term a³. The side a on the ruler is coral too.
the three slabs a × a × b, and the term 3a²b.
the three bars a × b × b, and the term 3ab².
the one b × b × b block, and the term b³. The side b on the ruler is aqua too.
the three planes that cut the cube, one per axis.

entries.title: Hardy–Weinberg as a square
entries.subject: biology
entries.claim: With random mating, one generation of offspring comes in the proportions p² + 2pq + q², drawn as a square, and the allele frequencies p and q are unchanged afterwards.
assumptions: one gene with two alleles, A and a
random mating in a large (effectively infinite) population
no mutation, no selection, no migration, no drift
the film shows one round with p = 3/5 and q = 2/5 (a 5 × 5 square of tiles); it is one worked case, not the general law

checks.what: the 30 A tokens and 20 a tokens span the same extents as the p and q rulers
checks.note: read back from the loaded scene and equal to the last digit

colour_key.means: allele A, its frequency p, and the AA pieces (p²).
the heterozygote Aa: the two gold pieces stacked under the middle term 2pq.
allele a, its frequency q, and the aa piece (q²).
labels, the cuts, and the two bins that count the alleles.

entries.title: Why cells are small
entries.subject: biology
entries.claim: For cubes, surface area divided by volume is 6, 3 and 2 for sides 1, 2 and 3, falling as 1 / side, so a bigger cell has less surface for each bit of interior.
assumptions: cells are idealised cubes built from an exact grid of unit cubes
ratios are per unit-cube width; SA / V ∝ 1 / side holds in any units
the folded membranes (cristae, alveoli) illustrate the idea; they are not measurements of real membranes

colour_key.means: the unit cubes that make each cell.
the skin: the surface of each cube, drawn as a see-through shell.
the single cube in the middle of the side-3 cube, the one farthest from the skin; also the numbers and the biology notes.
the folded membrane in the last scenes.
the readout of side, surface area, volume and their ratio.

entries.title: Two motions at once
entries.subject: physics
entries.claim: A thrown ball's path is two independent motions: constant horizontal speed, and vertical motion under constant gravity.
assumptions: no air resistance
constant gravity
flat ground, with launch and landing at one height
scene units, not SI: slow motion with g = 2.5 and a base speed of 6.32

checks.what: ball position against the closed form x = vx·t and y = 0.25 + vy·t − ½·g·t²
checks.note: five flights: 30°, 45° and 60° at speed 1, and 45° at speeds 0.75 and 1.25

colour_key.means: the sideways motion: the ground line, the ball's shadow on the ground, and the sideways arrow, which never changes.
the up-and-down motion: the pole, the bead on it, and the vertical arrow, which shrinks to nothing at the top.
gravity, whose arrow never changes.
the path: a dot every tenth of a second, a ring where the ball lands, and the arrow along the curve, which is the sum of the other two.

entries.title: A crank, a rod and a piston
entries.subject: mechanism
entries.claim: In a crank-slider the piston reaches its dead centers at the ends of the stroke, and the leverage of a steady push on the piston vanishes there and is largest near the middle of the stroke.
assumptions: rigid parts, no clearances, the piston line passes through the shaft
kinematics only: no friction, no inertia, no gas pressure
crank radius r = 1.2 and rod length l = 3.6 scene units, so l / r = 3; the quoted 58.6% and 1.05 r belong to that ratio
the steady push is a device for reading the leverage, not a model of a real cylinder

checks.what: crank pin, rod end, piston and leverage marker against the formulas
checks.note: across all eight turns of the crank; the crank pin agrees to 0.00001

colour_key.means: the dead centers: the rings and labels at the two ends of the stroke.
the crankshaft circle and the line the piston travels along.
the leverage: the stretched line on the rod, the gap, and its marker. The gap shrinks to nothing at the dead centers.
the steady push arrow on the piston (the lilac blocks under the cylinder are its stand).
